name: How do I compare primary bathroom remodeling bids correctly?

mainEntity.name: What should I look for when comparing multiple remodeling quotes so I do not choose the cheapest bad bid?
mainEntity.text: What should I look for when comparing multiple remodeling quotes so I do not choose the cheapest bad bid?

acceptedAnswer.text: The best way to compare primary bathroom remodeling bids is to make sure each contractor is pricing the same scope. One quote may include demolition, waterproofing, tile setting, fixtures, permits, and cleanup, while another may leave out major items or use vague allowances. The lowest number is not always the best value if it excludes key parts of the job. Ask what is included, what is excluded, and how changes are handled once the walls are open. For a primary bathroom, you should also verify whether the bid covers permit work, inspection coordination, waterproofing systems, and any premium fixture allowances. If one bid is dramatically lower than the others, that can be a warning sign. A clear, itemized proposal is usually more useful than a simple lump sum because it shows what you are actually buying.
acceptedAnswer.description: Compare bids by scope, not just price. Look for whether each quote includes demolition, waterproofing, permits, fixtures, tile allowances, labor, cleanup, inspections, and contingency for hidden issues. A very low bid often means something is missing, especially on custom primary bathroom projects.
